title: fix: hide agents excluded by operator roles from the picker
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes private agents appearing in the Control UI picker and agent directory when the signed-in user’s role allows only a subset of agents.

## User Impact

Users discover only agents allowed by their existing role. A saved selection falls back to an allowed agent; an empty allowlist clears the selection. Reloads and reconnects wait for current discovery instead of showing an older browser roster or remembered picker identity. Owners and roles with `agents: "*"` retain the full roster.

## Why This Change Was Made

Filter `agents.list` using the current operator role after asynchronous preparation, then reconcile UI selection against the returned roster. Preserve Gateway routing defaults and ownership metadata; existing session/run authorization stays enforced. Discovery does not grant or revoke session-reading access. Remove the cached discovery fallback and require a live roster for new-session catalog targets; keep stored sessions, groups, transcripts, and draft intent.

## Evidence

### Gateway filtering

Real isolated Gateway + Control UI, synthetic accounts, identical role configuration. Guest allows only `shared`; owner allows `*`. Baseline uses the exact changed modules from `4d8c9bddda7f992e293005b78f6bc1f8adea81ed`; candidate uses `9f53a63f3723452079ba2827895934a35031a8c4`. No mocked RPC responses or personal gateway data.

| Restricted user | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Desktop, 1440×900 | ![Before: guest sees private and main agents](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b087d2eb-b5bf-4090-b4cc-f9fb22ac8022) | ![After: guest sees only Shared Assistant](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/41586727-16c3-4a6a-99cf-b1a9214cb92e) |
| Mobile, 390×844 | ![Before: private agents appear in mobile picker](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/17e746c4-d7ef-4363-b4d3-0cf68f4ef425) | ![After: mobile picker exposes only allowed agent](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0e5f322e-0926-4434-9bae-8141a1594032) |

<details>
<summary>Owner and empty-allowlist controls</summary>

![Owner still sees the full roster](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/835a4dea-a3ab-4cb4-8b13-dad5d9cbc790)

![Empty allowlist returns no agents and clears the selection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f50d1798-2f2b-40e1-bd71-63fd194d1915)

</details>

- Real authenticated RPC assertions: restricted user receives only `["shared"]`; owner receives all three; empty allowlist receives `[]`. Both original browser runs passed; this Gateway code is unchanged by the cache repair.
- Gateway regressions: original handler **3 failed / 2 passed**; candidate **5 passed**. Covers subset, empty, wildcard, system owner, and role narrowing while catalog preparation is pending.
- UI selection suite: original behavior **3 failed / 38 passed**; candidate **41 passed**. Covers saved forbidden/default selection and loaded-empty roster behavior in both sidebar modes.
- Original Auto Review: no actionable P0–P2 findings; a later ClawSweeper review identified the persisted-roster gap addressed below.
- Changed-file repository checks **passed**, including core/test/UI type checks, lint, dead-export scans, import cycles, and all selected guards. Supplemental formatting/lint for the new gateway test also passed. All six original uploaded images were verified rendered on this PR.

<details>
<summary>Test cost and capture scope</summary>

`pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/agents-list.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`: **36.03s warm command wall, 38ms test bodies**. Cold wall was 164.43s, dominated by shared worker compilation. Only workspace/model roster enrichment is mocked; the handler and role resolver are real.

`ui/src/app/agent-selection.test.ts`: **5.48s command wall, under 50ms test bodies**. Browser proof is a local isolated integration run, not an added per-PR E2E suite (baseline 71.19s, candidate 106.82s scenario time).

Captured the actual sidebar picker on `/agents`, using synthetic trusted-proxy identities, disabled bundled plugins, and no mocked RPC responses. Desktop and mobile cover the changed rendered states. Owner and empty-role screenshots cover permission boundaries. The cache repair below additionally covers loading, reconnect, and failed-refresh states.

</details>

### Persisted-roster and reconnect regression

The later ClawSweeper P1 is fixed by removing persisted agent rosters from discovery and suppressing remembered picker identities without a current roster row. These additional captures run the real Control UI, bootstrap, localStorage version2 boot-record reader, and agent capability against a **synthetic WebSocket transport**. They prove the browser lifecycle; the original real-Gateway evidence above proves server filtering. Baseline freezes the ten affected production modules at `9f53a63f3723452079ba2827895934a35031a8c4`; candidate uses final source `a4ccc69f5815cbd2c790bfbd880e9ce6262787a3` (UI tree `ddcb19613aeb883ac46814c61ea82777f880f093`, refreshed after integrating the tested CI main parent). All accounts and content are synthetic.

The same credential/profile starts with an old three-agent boot record while live discovery is held. The restricted response admits only Shared Assistant. A later successful broader response is delivered through `config.changed`; the transport then reconnects after the role narrows and fails the new roster request. No application state is patched.

| Browser state | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Old version2 record; current roster pending | ![Before: cached private agents appear while discovery is pending](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/88baa555-72cd-4587-9245-acadcbfb5b87) | ![After: picker waits for current authorized discovery](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c2cdafb4-17e4-4101-8f17-83262d75e439) |
| Previously broader role; narrowed reconnect request fails | ![Before: broader roster returns after reconnect failure](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ec59587c-2600-4d8e-b3ca-4001af3f248a) | ![After: reconnect failure cannot restore the old roster](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3e554ea0-fdde-408d-a317-083ca3f94383) |

![After: successful current response shows only Shared Assistant](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0015b6e1-795a-435b-92e4-ca8a8612837d)

- All six browser lifecycle assertions pass on the candidate; five expose excluded agents on the baseline. The successful response still selects and displays the allowed agent.
- Regression-first proof: bootstrap/cache and failed-refresh cases failed before the repair; both now pass. Rendered picker-header regression failed before the repair and now passes for both pending and loaded-but-excluded discovery. Existing readable session labels remain visible.
- Focused lifecycle/route/sidebar run: 254 passed initially; the sole failure was an old attention fixture expecting an agent header with no roster. Supplying that fixture's live roster repairs its premise; the affected sidebar rerun passed 21/21. Adjacent selection, bootstrap selection, submit-gate, palette, and model-default suites passed 102/102.

Tradeoff: the agent directory and picker wait for live discovery after reload/reconnect. Cached conversation content and groups remain available; shorthand chat routes wait for hello routing defaults. No protocol, config, or stored-data schema change.

- Repair validation: all selected changed-file checks passed, including affected test/UI type checks, lint, format, and dead-export scans; the final attention-fixture format/lint supplement passed.
- Final full-diff AutoReview against the integrated CI main parent: **scoped-clean, no actionable P0–P2 findings**, covering the complete privacy change and cancellation repair below. Index and working-tree bytes matched during review.
### CI cancellation repair

[The failing CI job](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36778615037/job/110103271158) exposed a pre-existing Stop race, also reproduced on its unmodified main parent `8c39234ebfff5ce5643bf3c9ee544ecac67e7705`. A concurrent cancellation metadata write temporarily invalidated session facts between the terminal registry commit and publication, leaving the scheduler slot active.

The three-file repair uses the existing session publication FIFO around native persistence, acknowledgement, and publication. Snapshot capture/restore stays synchronous; transcript/plugin work and terminal cleanup stay outside the FIFO. Current-owner, generation, retirement, and replacement checks remain enforced. The original CI main parent was integrated specifically to repair this owner; the mechanical merge tree matches the inspected CI merge exactly.

| Local regression proof | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Exact original 50-file CI plan | 953 passed, 3 skipped, 2 failed; 152.70s | 955 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed; 134.55s |
| Real Stop fixture | 10 passed, 2 failed; 47.38s | 12 passed; 39.30s |
| Two new held-admission regressions | Both fail; 5.27s command wall | Full owner suite 21 passed; 2.27s command wall, new cases 4ms/3ms |

The new cases prove staged terminal rows remain private while metadata publication is held, then publish for the current owner and refuse a replaced owner. These are local results; current-head hosted CI remains enforced by the normal landing workflow.

Selected final checks passed: repository guards, core production types, all 27 test type graphs, all three unused-export scans, scoped lint, format, import cycles, and storage/auth guards. Lint found two redundant default type arguments in the new test; those were removed and scoped lint/format plus all 21 publication tests passed again (3.24s wrapper wall). No behavioral source changed after the clean AutoReview.

### Reconnect drafts and final browser regressions

Live-only discovery also retires the settings editor's selected target during reconnect. Preserve its unsaved identity draft privately and restore it only when current discovery re-admits the same agent for the same profile and selection intent. Source/profile changes and a newer selection discard it. The page's draft-retention owner keeps discovery and actions unavailable while the roster is absent.

Real Control UI against the existing synthetic Gateway fixture, identical interrupted-save scenario. Baseline is `a4ccc69f5815cbd2c790bfbd880e9ce6262787a3`; candidate is `607311074a83df2a9ee300c02f1d0d43170709db`. The typed name is lost before the repair and retained after live rediscovery.

| After reconnect interrupts saving | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Unsaved identity edit | ![Before: reconnect loses the unsaved agent name](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/95b02d67-1653-460c-8947-b8b4799a2858) | ![After: reconnect preserves the unsaved agent name](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/74154509-517f-49bc-8c88-95d87331b895) |

| Focused local regression proof | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Same-target identity draft + rejection controls | Same-target fails; 4 rejection controls pass, 1.82s | Full selection/identity suites: 28 pass, 1.40s |
| Save interrupted at update/config read | 2 fail, 18.25s | 2 pass, 13.94s |
| Sidebar fixture prerequisites | 3 fail, 3.52s | Both affected suites: 256 pass, 29.03s |
| Memory import failed roster then explicit retry | Original case fails, 2.94s | Complete suite: 12 pass, 2.52s; revised case 78ms |
| New-session live workspace defaults | Explicit-folder case fails, 29.52s | Complete browser file: 4 pass, 22.96s; changed cases 3.96s/4.05s |
| Qualified warm-reload conversation | Original matching-profile case fails, 22.46s | All 4 profile cases pass, 17.82s |

The reconnect cases retain their original assertions. New-session now exercises live roster admission before explicit workspace selection, then holds discovery during reconnect to verify draft retention and blocked dispatch. Warm reload uses a literal conversation key so the test retains its pre-hello transcript/auth-isolation contract; shorthand main routes intentionally require live routing defaults. The draft extraction also shrinks the existing settings page, with the repository size guard passing. These are local command wall times; hosted timing remains visible in the linked CI run.

The earlier CI run also reported a single 120s mobile GitHub-hovercard timeout. Its test and owning hovercard/registration code are unchanged by this PR. An original-order replay of all 21 cases passed in34.83s; this is a non-reproduction, not a repair. CI diagnostics suggest the deferred preview request was never observed after mobile resize/focus, but did not preserve the failing page state, so the cause remains unresolved. No assertion, timeout, or retry policy was weakened; final-head CI remains required.

Independent incremental AutoReview completed at P0–P2 with one suggestion, inspected and rejected: discard a retained local draft when the same operator keeps read access but loses identity-write permission. The draft contains that operator’s own typed input and is restored only for a currently discoverable agent; preserving it does not grant write access. Existing overview controls remain disabled without `agents.update` authority, and `saveIdentityDraft` checks current `operator.admin` permission both at entry and immediately before dispatch. Clearing the draft would introduce avoidable data loss rather than repair an authorization leak. No accepted actionable findings remain.

Follow-up selected checks passed: repository guards, all 8 affected test type graphs, UI types, i18n, three unused-export scans, formatting, scoped lint, and stylelint. Lint identified a shadowed callback variable; its local name was changed without affecting behavior, followed by passing format/lint/stylelint.

### Inherited cancellation fixture failure

The final Node shard on `a4ccc69` stalled in `chat.abort-errors.test.ts` (`cascade native new`), then the reset/delete cases failed cleanup. The original-order 10-case file reproduces 7 passes and 3 failures both on the tested merge `75b750f9` and its unmodified main parent `b09d30a`, using bounded diagnostic timeouts. The fixture held a child metadata writer while waiting for terminal publication through that same writer queue.

Main already contains the canonical repair [79f0e9bf127](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/79f0e9bf1271ec2b40abb00402c6a4d89cba1330): hold the original abort-marker call after termination, then delegate to the real helper, preserving all lifecycle/transcript assertions. Its published validation reports 10/10 focused cases and 424/424 in the original 31-file group on Linux. No duplicate fixture change or production adjustment is added here; current-head CI must exercise the PR with that main fix.

Receiving validation of canonical `79f0e9bf127`: the unchanged 10-case abort/reset file passes on the previously failing exact PR merge with only the canonical test blob applied, using normal configured budgets (73.51s test duration / 76.73s command wall). The formerly stalled native-new/reset/delete cases take 1.59s / 1.94s / 2.92s. This is local receiving proof; current-head hosted CI remains required.
